Elena — thanks for the quick clarifications. I attached a short worked example (FintechX_unit_econ_model.xlsx) but pulling the key points into the email so you have them in-line: 

Assumptions (conservative / example)
- Pilot: 1.5M tokens/mo; Prod: 10M tokens/mo
- Redwood estimated marginal inference cost (inc. GPU amortization, batching, bandwidth): ~$18 per 1M tokens
- Redwood proposed list price scenarios: $45 / $1M, $60 / $1M, $90 / $1M
- Target gross margin we typically aim for on inference: 60–75% (varies by commitment/SLAs)

Per-scenario economics (monthly, at 10M tokens)
- At $45 / 1M tokens: Revenue = $450 / month? (note: that's $45 * 10 = $450) — wait check units: actually $45/1M * 10M = $450 monthly. Annualized = $5,400.
- Cost @ $18 / 1M = $180 monthly; Gross margin = (450-180)/450 = 60%
- At $60 / 1M: Revenue = $600 monthly; Cost = $180 monthly; Gross margin = 70%
- At $90 / 1M: Revenue = $900 monthly; Cost = $180 monthly; Gross margin = 80%

CAC payback example (simple model)
- FintechX quoted ARR target for year one: $150k (midpoint of your range).
- If deal ARR = $150k, and Redwood annual gross margin at $60/1M on expected volume gives 70%:
  - Annual gross profit from inference = $150k * 0.70 = $105k
  - If our sales/SE CAC for this deal is estimated at $30k, payback = CAC / (annual gross profit) = 30k / 105k ≈ 0.29 years (≈ 3.5 months)

Notes on the math and why numbers look low in the worked example: 
- The per-1M figure multiplies directly by volume; make sure we’re aligned on whether your teams report tokens/month per user or tokens/month overall for product.
- Our quoted "cost" line above is Redwood's estimated marginal cost to serve; committed reserved capacity or dedicated pools can reduce marginals further (we can model that).

Requested next items from FintechX
1) Confirm whether the 10M tokens is total monthly across all customers or the estimated consumption for a single high-volume customer (this changes ARR math).
2) Share expected ARR target for year 1 (you gave range; a single number helps finalize the quote).
3) Confirm procurement timeline for SOC 2 + contract redlines.

I’ll plan to run a short sensitivity table in the workbook mapping: tokens/month x price per 1M x CAC scenarios -> payback months and gross margin. Happy to present on the follow-up call.

Best,
Marissa
